name: Edie Hooton

summary.text: Edie Hooton represented Boulder's state House District 10 from 2017 to 2023 and has served on the legislature's Capital Development Committee, which oversees capital funding for Colorado's public higher-education institutions.

experience.text: Chaired the legislature's Capital Development Committee and served as vice chair of the Energy and Environment Committee, 2021-2022.
Master of Public Administration, University of Pennsylvania, 1993.

education_focus.text: Hooton says her top priorities are holding the line on in-state tuition amid a projected $2 billion state budget deficit, improving four-year graduation rates, and ensuring transparency in university budgeting.

She says she would not commit CU to Trump administration policies that 'threaten academic freedom, diversity, or institutional autonomy' and would instead help build a multistate coalition to defend the university's funding and curricula.
On affordability, she proposes curbing administrative costs, locking tuition rates for incoming freshmen, expanding concurrent and hybrid enrollment, and funding campus housing.

positions.quote: I fully embrace the call for 100% renewable energy by 2030 – it is what is needed to respond to the climate crisis facing our planet
positions.note: From Hooton's 2016 Colorado House campaign website as archived by Ballotpedia; only the year is shown, not an exact date. This predates her 2026 CU Regent run and no more recent statement on this topic was found.

positions.source_title: CU Board of Regents candidates answer questions on tuition, AI and federal oversight
positions.quote: Using my legislative experience, I will partner with state allies — leveraging successful strategies like Attorney General Weiser’s multi-state lawsuits and Denver federal court rulings that halted attacks on Boulder’s NCAR — to aggressively protect CU.
positions.note: Hooton names the state attorney general's multi-state lawsuits against federal actions as a strategy she would use to protect CU, rather than making a general statement about all state litigation against the administration.
